literal: Having their secrets detected, by the local townspeople they will be laughed at always, those who drink liquor secretly and lose their awareness.
translation: Those who drink liquor secretly and lose their senses will have their secrets found out and will be laughed at by their fellow-townsmen at all times.
modern: ரகசியமாகக் கள் குடித்துத் தன் அறிவை இழப்பவர்கள், எப்போதும் தம் ஊர் மக்களால் அவர்களின் ரகசியங்கள் அறியப்பட்டு எள்ளி நகையாடப்படுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the illusion of secret drinking. The poet explains that those who drink liquor in secret ('kaḷ oṟṟi') and lose their mental clarity or droop their eyes ('kaṇ cāypavar') cannot keep it a secret for long. Their inner secrets will be easily detected ('uḷ oṟṟi') by others because of their drunken behavior. Consequently, they will be mocked and laughed at ('nakappaṭuvar') by their own local townspeople ('uḷḷūr') at all times ('eññāṉṟum').
